paper.title: How to sample and when to stop sampling: The generalized Wald problem and minimax policies

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Wald problem under diffusion asymptotics (continuous time, Gaussian increments)
unmapped: continuous time: signals dx_a = mu_a pi_a dt + sigma_a sqrt(pi_a) dW_a
flow sampling cost c per unit time; learner chooses an adaptive stopping time tau and pays c*tau
objective is minimax (max over means) expected regret = simple-regret-type loss of the implemented arm plus sampling cost
arm variances sigma_1^2, sigma_0^2 are known; learner knows the cost c
settings.definition_quote: V\left(\bm{d},\bm{\mu}\right) :=\mathbb{E}_{\bm{d}\vert\bm{\mu}}\left[\max\{\mu_{1}-\mu_{0},0\}-(\mu_{1}-\mu_{0})\delta+c\tau\right]. ... the DM conducts a sequential experiment, while paying a flow cost $c$ as long as the experiment is in progress.

settings.name_in_paper: Best arm identification (two arms) under diffusion asymptotics, tau = 1
unmapped: continuous-time diffusion limit with fixed experiment duration tau=1 (corresponds to n observations)
settings.definition_quote: The best arm identification problem is a special case of the generalized Wald problem where the stopping time is fixed beforehand and set to $\tau=1$ without loss of generality.

settings.name_in_paper: Generalized Wald problem in parametric regimes with small cost asymptotics
unmapped: per-observation sampling cost C = c/n^{3/2}, small-cost asymptotics n -> infinity
local alternatives theta_0 + h/sqrt(n) with equal reference means; regret scaled by sqrt(n)
learner chooses adaptive stopping time bounded by T
learner knows score functions, information matrices I_a and mean derivatives (sigma_a^2 = mu_dot' I^-1 mu_dot) and the cost c
settings.definition_quote: the DM experiments sequentially in periods $j=1,2,\dots$ after paying an `effective sampling cost' $C$ per period... small cost asymptotics, wherein $C=c/n^{3/2}$ for some $c\in(0,\infty)$, and $n\to\infty$.

algorithms.name: Minimax decision rule d* (Neyman allocation + threshold stopping on x1/sigma1 - x0/sigma0)
d_{n,T}: finite-sample Neyman allocation with stopping when |rho_n(t)| >= gamma*
d*_BAI: Neyman allocation with implementation of arm with higher standardized signal

source.label: theorem=0000201
source.quote: The zero-sum two player game (\ref{eq:def of minimax risk}) has a Nash equilibrium with a unique minimax-regret value. The minimax-regret optimal decision rule is $\bm{d}^{*}:=(\pi^{*},\tau^{*},\delta^{*})$, where $\pi_{a}^{*}(t)=\sigma_{a}/(\sigma_{1}+\sigma_{0})$ ... Furthermore, the least-favorable prior is a symmetric two-point distribution supported on $(\sigma_{1}\Delta^{*}/2,-\sigma_{0}\Delta^{*}/2),(-\sigma_{1}\Delta^{*}/2,\sigma_{0}\Delta^{*}/2)$.

results.notes: The theorem characterises the optimal rule; the explicit value (sigma_1+sigma_0)/2 R(gamma*,Delta*) is from the proof, and the scaling by eta follows from the proof of Lemma 3 (R scales linearly in eta). Quantity is max-regret including sampling cost.

source.label: Lemma=0000202
source.quote: Suppose $\bm{\mu}$ is such that $\vert\mu_{1}-\mu_{0}\vert=\frac{\sigma_{1}+\sigma_{0}}{2}\Delta$. Then, for any $\gamma,\Delta>0$, $V(\tilde{\bm{d}}_{\gamma},\bm{\mu})=\frac{(\sigma_{1}+\sigma_{0})}{2}\Delta\frac{1-e^{-\Delta\gamma}}{e^{\Delta\gamma}-e^{-\Delta\gamma}}+\frac{2c\gamma}{\Delta}\frac{e^{\Delta\gamma}+e^{-\Delta\gamma}-2}{e^{\Delta\gamma}-e^{-\Delta\gamma}}$.

results.notes: Exact frequentist regret (incl. sampling cost) of the threshold rule family d_gamma, which includes d* at gamma=gamma*.

conditions: two arms, known variances, experiment duration tau=1
